decision_conditions: The vehicle crossover, by virtue of the loss of the boundary wall, the street tree, and grass verge to the front of the property, would cause an unacceptable level of visual harm to the character and appearance of the streetscene at Berkeley Close. As such, the proposed development represents a clear policy conflict with Policy BE 1 of The Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies (2012), and Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), and policy contained within the National Planning Policy Framework.

The proposed development, by reason of the insufficient dimensions of the proposed parking space, would fail to provide a usable off-street parking space in accordance with the Council's adopted parking standards. The development would result in the loss of on-street parking capacity through the formation of a vehicle crossover without providing a compliant replacement parking space within the site, to the detriment of local parking provision and highway safety. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).
